final_answer:
**Supported facts**

The latest official Bun release I found is **`Bun v1.4`**, and the official GitHub releases page marks it as **`Latest`** with tag **`bun-v1.4.0`**. (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases)

Its official Bun blog release post is dated **August 20, 2026**. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4) The official GitHub release entry also shows it was released on **August 20** at **14:07**. (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases)

According to Bun’s official release post, the headline changes in Bun 1.4 are:
- **A major Node.js compatibility jump**: Bun 1.4 adds **1,517** Node.js test-suite passes, which Bun calls its **biggest jump in Node.js compatibility since Bun 1.0**. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **Large production/runtime improvements**: Bun says Bun 1.4 **fixes over 2,900 issues**, **reduces idle CPU usage by 5x**, **reduces memory usage by up to 35%**, and **starts 50% faster on Linux**. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **A rewrite from Zig to Rust**: the release post says Bun 1.4 **rewrites Bun from Zig to Rust**, and later states that Bun is now written in Rust and that this is the **first release** of that rewrite. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **A much larger built-in standard library / fewer external dependencies**: Bun says this release makes its built-in standard library bigger, lists **15 dependencies now built in**, and says these features ship in the Bun binary with **no install step, no native build, and no lockfile entry**. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **New built-in APIs and commands** highlighted at the top of the release include **`Bun.Image`**, **`Bun.WebView`**, **`Bun.markdown`**, **`Bun.cron()`**, **`Bun.Terminal`**, **`bun run --parallel`**, **`bun test --parallel`**, **`bun audit fix`**, **`bun dedupe`**, and **`bun prune`**. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)

Official release-note details for some of those additions:
- **`Bun.Image`** is a built-in image library for decode/resize/rotate/encode workflows, with no native addon required. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **`Bun.WebView`** is built-in headless browser automation, without Puppeteer or Playwright. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **`bun run --parallel`** runs multiple `package.json` scripts concurrently and Bun says it replaces tools like `npm-run-all` and `concurrently`. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)

**Inference**

“**Latest stable release**” is slightly interpretive here. I did **not** find an official Bun page, in the sources I checked, that explicitly says “Bun 1.4.0 is the latest stable release.” What I did find is:
- Bun 1.0 was the release where Bun said it was **stable and production-ready**. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.0)
- The official GitHub releases page marks **`bun-v1.4.0`** as **`Latest`**. (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases)

So the best-supported conclusion is: **the latest stable Bun release is Bun 1.4.0**, inferred from Bun’s stable 1.x line and GitHub’s official `Latest` marker. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.0, https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases)

“**Most consequential changes**” is also a judgment call. My ranking is an **inference** from what Bun emphasizes most prominently in its official Bun 1.4 release post: the Rust rewrite, the Node.js compatibility jump, the large CPU/memory/startup improvements, and the expansion of built-in APIs/tools. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4)

**Disagreement / uncertainty / lack of good evidence**

I found **no disagreement** between Bun’s official blog and Bun’s official GitHub releases page about the current release: both point to **Bun 1.4 / bun-v1.4.0**. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4, https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases)

The main **uncertainty** is terminological, not version-related: the official sources I checked clearly establish **latest official release**, but they do not, in the pages I used, separately define a distinct “stable” channel for Bun 1.4.0 beyond Bun’s already-stable 1.x release line. (https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.0, https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases)
